text.p: These are the highlights of the main Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro newspapers this morning.
GAZETA MERCANTIL
-- UNITED STATES REDOUBLES PROTEST AGAINST CAR RULES

Prompting discomfort in the Brazilian government, the United States on Tuesday decided to open an investigation into Brazil's auto import rules. Argentina, Australia and Indonesia also were included on Washington's probe list.
-- 100 MILLION WILL CHOOSE THEIR MAYORS

More than 100 million Brazilian voters will go to the polls Thursday to choose mayors and municipal council members and 32.4 percent of them will be casting electronic ballots in the first test of the new technology in Brazil.
-- PRIVATE PENSION FIRM BRASILPREV EXPANDS ITS PARTNERSHIP
Brasilprev, the country's second-largest private pension firm whose products are distributed through Banco do Brasil, is poised to forge partnerships with other banks, its president Fuad Noman said.
O GLOBO
-- LEADING RIO MAYOR CANDIDATE HOSPITALIZED WITH ULCER

Rio de Janeiro mayoral candidate Luiz Conde, who is leading in the polls, was hospitalized Tuesday with a gastric ulcer, according to a medical report. Conde's condition is not serious but he is to remain in the hospital 48 hours.
-- U.S. OPENS PROBE INTO BRAZILIAN IMPORT QUOTAS

The United States on Tuesday began an investigation into barriers created by the Brazilian government against foreign car imports. Brazil could suffer trade retaliation if the dispute is not resolved within 60 days.
-- ELECTIONS BOARD SLAMS RELEASE OF POLLS ON EVE OF VOTE

The head of Brazil's elections board, Marco Aurelio de Mello, criticized the publication of opinion polls on the eve of nationwide municipal elections, saying some 40 percent of voters are influenced by the last-minute surveys.
FOLHA DE SAO PAULO
-- MAYORAL CAMPAIGN IN SAO PAULO ENDS UP IN TRIBUNALS
Brazil's Supreme Electoral Tribunal suspended Sao Paulo mayoral candidate Celso Pitta's right to air campaign ads rebutting last-minute accusations made by his opponents.
-- SAO PAULO MAYOR CANDIDATE'S CAMPAIGN PHONES TAPPED

Eavesdropping devices were discovered on two telephone lines used by the front-running Sao Paulo mayoral candidate Celso Pitta's electoral committee. Police are investigating the incident but have not turned up any suspect yet.
-- U.S. MAY SANCTION BRAZIL OVER AUTO IMPORT RULES
The United States has begun a probe and may seek sanctions against Brazil over its automobile import policy, which it considers protectionist.
Reuters has not verified the stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
-- James Craig, Sao Paulo newsroom 5511 232 4411
